newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian in Aussie cash case asked to bare assets.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian in Aussie cash case asked to bare assets.

text.p: Malaysia's opposition leader on Friday asked a government chief minister to publicly declare his assets after the man was arrested in Australia for trying to take nearly money out of the country without permission.
Muhammad Muhammad Taib has created a "notorious record" as the first chief minister of a Malaysian state to be arrested and charged in a foreign country, Lim Kit Siang said.

Muhammad, chief minister for the central Selangor state, was stopped at Australia's Brisbane airport on Sunday while trying to leave for New Zealand with about A$1.2 million ($960,000) in Malaysian, Singaporean and New Zealand dollars.
Under Australian law, people leaving the country must declare and justify any amount worth over A$5,000 taken out, in whatever currency.
Prime Minister Mahathir Mohammad has asked Muhammad to give him a report on the incident, officials in Kuala Lumpur said.
Muhammad also is a vice-president of Mahathir's United Malays National Organisation, the dominant political party in Malaysia.
Lim, chief of the opposition Democratic Action Party (DAP), said in a statement that Muhammad should publicly declare his assets in the last 10 years while serving as chief minister.

"The conflicting versions as to the ownership and purpose of the...cash found on Muhammad's person at the Brisbane airport has only highlighted the imperative need for Muhammad to give a full and satisfactory accounting," Lim said.
Malaysia's acting foreign minister Abu Hassan Omar said on Thursday that the money found on Muhammad was his own and was meant for "shopping". But the chief minister's office in Selangor denied this.

Muhammad was released unconditionally by Brisbane police after the arrest but has to reappear in the Australian city for a hearing on March 31. Malaysian officials said he was currently in New Zealand.
